items.rule: Well to septic system and its leaching field (where septic water drains into the soil), buried oil tank, or other pollution source
items.condition: Well with a required withdrawal rate under 10 gpm — the band a single-family home sits in.
items.scales: Bands follow the well's required withdrawal rate (what it serves), not its tested yield: 150 ft if the supply must deliver 10-50 gpm (e.g. one well serving several homes), 200 ft above 50 gpm. A single home sits in the under-10 band.
items.finding: We can't measure your lot from public records — your surveyor or engineer confirms these distances on the site plan, and the health district checks them in the field before filing.

items.rule: Well to surface water (high-water mark) / surface-water or foundation drain
items.condition: Well with a required withdrawal rate under 10 gpm.
items.scales: Bands follow the well's required withdrawal rate (what it serves), not its tested yield: 150 ft if the supply must deliver 10-50 gpm (e.g. one well serving several homes), 200 ft above 50 gpm. A single home sits in the under-10 band.

items.rule: Well to tight-joint sewer (extra-heavy cast iron, leaded joints, or equal)
items.condition: Tight-joint sewer only; well with a required withdrawal rate under 10 gpm.
items.scales: Bands follow the well's required withdrawal rate (what it serves), not its tested yield: 150 ft if the supply must deliver 10-50 gpm (e.g. one well serving several homes), 200 ft above 50 gpm. A single home sits in the under-10 band.

items.rule: Well to the leaching system (where septic water drains into the soil) IF the soil is fast AND the ledge is shallow — the distance doubles
items.condition: Applies when BOTH hold: soil percolation rate faster than 1.0 minute per inch, AND the bottom of the leaching system is less than 8 ft above ledge rock. For a single-family home the 75 ft distance becomes 150 ft. Only soil tests on the lot can settle whether this applies — it cannot be screened from public data.
items.source: CT DPH Technical Standards for Subsurface Sewage Disposal Systems, Table 1 Item A (applied to wells via Reg. 19-13-B102d)
